source.title: Less is More: Local Intrinsic Dimensions of Contextual Language Models
source.authors: Benjamin Matthias Ruppik; Julius von Rohrscheidt; Carel van Niekerk; Michael Heck; Renato Vukovic; Shutong Feng; Hsien-Chin Lin; Nurul Lubis; Bastian Rieck; Marcus Zibrowius; Milica Gavsi'c

record.tranche_reason: The study trains a small transformer on modular addition with different training-data fractions and tracks training and held-out accuracy over extended training, explicitly using the original grokking setup. It also measures local dimensions over training to relate their changes to generalization.
record.gate_note: The relevant new results are in Section 4.2 and Figures 2 and 16. The discussion of grokking in the introduction and cited results from other work are not recorded as findings. The paper describes accuracy and dimension trends in prose for groups of fractions; individual plotted values are not stated numerically.
record.test_reason: The study reruns the Power et al. modular-addition setup (p = 197, 10–50% training fractions, AdamW with weight decay) and reports training and validation accuracy over extended training. These are its own results on whether delayed generalization occurs (V1). The local-intrinsic-dimension signal is a geometric measure, not a circuit or memorization analysis, so it is recorded under fits_no_version rather than V2.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that a drop in mean local dimension on training data strongly indicates generalization in this modular-addition setting, coinciding with the rise in validation accuracy. Their abstract and conclusion go further, claiming that dimensionality anticipates grokking onset and that reductions accompany and predict later performance gains across tasks. They also state that a causal link remains open.
record.recipe_differences: The paper says it keeps the original modular-addition setup; it adds local intrinsic-dimension measurements. It also varies training fractions from 10% to 50%.
record.method_sensitivity: Grokking outcome depends on training-data fraction and individual training-run seed; the onset varies greatly across individual seeds. Grokking was not seen for the 10% and 15% fractions within the reported training period.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean local intrinsic dimension of training-set embeddings rises early, then drops when validation accuracy starts rising in grokking runs. It stays flat in non-grokking runs. LID–validation-accuracy Spearman correlations are 0.076 and 0.257 at 10% and 15%, and negative for fractions ≥20%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An unsupervised geometric signal (a drop in local intrinsic dimension on training data) coincides with, and may anticipate, the onset of grokking.

record.peer_reviewed: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, Volume 38 (NeurIPS 2025)
record.problems: The grokking results are averaged over 5 seeds per configuration, and individual seeds show substantial variation in onset. Accuracy outcomes are reported on a validation split, not a test split. The main results cover 60 000 batches; no quantified dataset-size versus delay relationship is reported.

untested.parts: No quantified relation between training fraction and delay length. Accuracy is on a validation split (the held-out remainder). Only the first 60k of a 400k-step schedule is shown.
No circuit identification, Fourier analysis, or measurement of memorization removal. LID is a related geometric signal, not V2's mechanism.

missing.what: Per-seed runs show that the onset of grokking varies greatly across seeds. This bears on how reliable the delay is for V1.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V1 'challenges' label for the 10% and 15% fractions is removed. V1 does not claim grokking at every fraction within a fixed horizon, and a longer delay at smaller data is what V1 predicts. The V2 labels are removed because LID is not V2's circuit or memorization measure. Neither original source is this study.

versions.untested_parts: Uses validation accuracy rather than test accuracy. It does not report a quantified relation between training-set fraction and the number of optimization steps required for grokking.
Measures mean local dimension as a progress signal, but does not identify a generalizing circuit, analyze Fourier algorithms, or measure memorizing components being removed.

relationships.condition: modular addition p=197, training fractions ≥20%, within 60k steps, 5 seeds
relationships.reason: Training accuracy saturates quickly (r3-r7) while validation accuracy lags, then reaches near-perfect levels (r10-r14). Smaller fractions do not generalize in the window (r8-r9), consistent with a longer delay.
relationships.display_finding: Training accuracy saturated quickly and validation later became near-perfect at training fractions of at least 20%, while smaller fractions failed to generalize within 60,000 steps.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Training accuracy becomes almost perfect while validation accuracy lags and later reaches almost perfect levels in runs described as grokking (r3-r7, r10-r14).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: training fractions 0.1 and 0.15, within the selected training horizon
reader_labels.reason: Despite nearly perfect training accuracy, validation accuracy does not rise beyond the training-data fraction in the reported period (r1-r2, r8-r9).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The training-set mean local dimension drops as validation accuracy begins to rise, and the dimension-accuracy correlations are negative for these runs (r17-r21, r24).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: In non-grokking runs, mean local dimension rises and then stays mostly flat; its correlation with validation accuracy is weak relative to training accuracy (r15-r16, r22-r23).
